historical_references.reference: Modestina of Capua was a Christian martyr who lived during the late 3rd or early 4th century. According to legend, she was a wealthy matron who used her wealth to help the poor and convert many to Christianity. When the governor of Capua, Capito, learned of her activities, he ordered her to renounce her faith. She refused, and was subjected to various forms of torture, including being burnt at the stake. She is believed to have been killed by the sword, and her remains were buried in a tomb outside the city walls.

Saint Modestus or Modestina is mentioned in the 'Acts of the Martyrs of Abitinae' as a martyr who lived during the time of Emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD). According to the account, she was a slave in a villa near Abitinae, who was converted to Christianity by Saint Felicissimus and Saint Agapius. She refused to renounce her faith, and was subjected to various forms of torture, including being thrown into a cauldron of boiling water. She survived and was eventually beheaded. Her relics were later translated to Milan, where they are venerated in the Basilica of San Lorenzo.
